answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to multiply by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashing stake before it can submit jobs or earn trust. A lantern-style registry records signed actions against that stake, while peers rate completed work; proven fraud burns the deposit and lowers the linked reputation. One attacker can still create many names, but each must tie up capital and survive scrutiny, so Sybil scale becomes expensive rather than free. Neither a tundra nor yarrow changes the rule: identity count alone grants no credibility.
